da-non-sequitur.evidence: (S↔P column of prop:hecke-baer-star-generic row) Main: ref `…HeckeBaerStarGeneric.hecke_baer_star_generic` names no declaration (library file is "intentionally empty"; the sibling has `hecke_baer_star_generic_sketch`), and that sketch rests on axioms. Under open PR #7915: the PR proves `matrix_algebra_baer_right`, removes the false axiom `hecke_baer_star_generic_sketch_axiom` (refuted over 𝔽₂ with transpose) and repoints the ref to the refutation `not_hecke_baer_star_generic_sketch` — so after merge the statement is still unbacked (the PR's own note says the positive-star version is open). Proof/statement errors the PR does not touch: (1) Step 1 is false: bar(e_(2)) = e_(2), not e_(1,1). In H₂, e_(2) = (σ+q⁻¹)/(q+q⁻¹) and e_(1,1) = (q−σ)/(q+q⁻¹) are each bar-fixed (sympy, using σ⁻¹ = σ − (q−q⁻¹)). (2) The boxed failure locus is wrong both ways. It includes q = ±1 (q⁴ = 1), where H_n(±1) is semisimple in char 0. It also says "equivalently primitive 2k-th roots", which drops q = ζ₃: there [3]_q = ζ₃⁻²+1+ζ₃² = 0, so H₃(ζ₃) is not semisimple, yet ζ₃ is not a primitive 2k-th root for any k. (3) Step 3, "every idempotent is similar to a self-adjoint one", needs a positive (proper) involution. The bar involution is not shown to be one, and PR #7915's 𝔽₂ counterexample shows the step fails without it. (4) For an arbitrary char-0 field R there is no antilinear q ↦ q⁻¹ (e.g. R = ℚ, q = 2). (5) The converse ("fails exactly where non-semisimple") is not proved

trap-superlative.notes: Flagged for the coordinating session, three items, none edited (all math): (1) Step 1's stated reason is checkably wrong. "The eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of sigma_i are swapped by *: q -> q^{-1}." Under q -> q^{-1} the value q becomes q^{-1} and -q^{-1} becomes -q; neither is the other member of the pair {q, -q^{-1}}. The map that swaps them is q -> -q^{-1}, which is the OTHER Hecke involution - the one that does induce lambda -> lambda' on Wedderburn blocks. The bar involution as defined in the proposition (sigma_i -> sigma_i^{-1}, q -> q^{-1}) is the Kazhdan-Lusztig bar, which preserves each block. So the conclusion *(e_lambda) = e_{lambda'} does not follow from the reason given, and may need the other involution. Scope (a): this is a defect in the stated justification, not a proof that the conclusion is false. (2) Step 3 assumes "algebraically closed R" and the displayed Wedderburn decomposition needs a splitting field, but the proposition only hypothesises a field of characteristic 0. Hypothesis mismatch. (3) "d_lambda is the dimension of the lambda-isotypic component" - d_lambda is dim V_lambda (the SYT count); the isotypic component has dimension d_lambda^2, which is what M_{d_lambda}(R) has.

trap-nonspeakable.evidence: Proof prose is plain; no noun-chains.
